challenge_title: One place, and a memory that lasts
challenge:
Tasks usually live in one app, notes in another, health and learning in a third. Worse, anything that happened months ago is effectively gone: nobody can find it, and no assistant knows it.

We built one system from scratch with a single long-term memory at its heart, an Obsidian knowledge base, and an AI agent that lives inside it. It talks to the user where they already are: in Telegram.
built_intro: A backend, a web app, a Telegram assistant and a knowledge base that ties them together.

built.title: A permanent memory in Obsidian
built.text: Every task, note and conversation lands in an Obsidian vault configured across platforms. Nothing is lost, and everything is connected in one knowledge graph.

built.title: A Telegram assistant
built.text: Answers questions, plans the day, sets reminders, listens to voice messages and runs analyses. It briefs the user in the morning and reviews the evening and the week.

built.title: A web app
built.text: A daily view, upcoming items, all tasks, projects, goals and areas of life, with the same data the bot works with.

built.title: Health and learning
built.text: Health tracking with Apple Health, and a learning area for language study.

built.title: Claude under the hood
built.text: The assistant runs on the Claude API from Anthropic, with the vault as its knowledge and memory.

built.title: Cost control
built.text: Daily and monthly limits on the AI budget: the bot refuses model calls past the cap.

ai_text: The agent lives inside the knowledge base. When the user asks about something from months ago, it searches the vault and finds it, then plans, answers, listens to voice messages and runs analyses on top of that memory. It works with the user’s own data, inside a spending cap.
